verdicts.title: Privacy-auditing tutorial prices a shuffled fixed-batch DataLoader with Poisson amplification and under-counts its own steps
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link. docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb cell 9 trains with `DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` (fixed-size shuffled batches, no Opaque sampler, drop_last=False), and cell 13 prices it with `sample_rate = batch_size/len(train_data)` and `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data)//batch_size)` fed into `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(0.5), sample_rate) * total_steps`. Shuffled fixed-size batching is not Poisson subsampling (independent per-record inclusion), and the floor division drops the last partial batch the loader actually yields. Ran the notebook's own constants against HEAD's .venv: coin_flip(num_canaries=500, key=key(42)) yields len(cf.train_subset(dataset)) = 252 (the committed output says 263), len(train_loader) = 4, so the loop runs 800 steps while the notebook computes 200*(252//64) = 600. Epsilons at delta=1e-5: 250.89 at the documented 600 steps, 314.46 at the 800 actually run, 519.70 with no amplification at all (200 participations) - the published number is the smallest of the three. Contrast verified: docs/tutorials/dp_sgd_training.ipynb cell 13 was fixed to iterate `PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=..., n_steps=total_steps, key=key(43))` with the comment 'The sampler and accountant use the same independent-inclusion process'. .github/workflows/pr.yml:290-302 executes only accounting_and_calibration.ipynb, dp_sgd_training.ipynb and dp_ftrl_training.ipynb, so nothing runs this notebook. Not tracked: the issue that subsumed OPQ-355 (#843, 'Sweep A - regenerate and execute every documented accounting snippet', which names exactly quickstart.md + dp_sgd_training.ipynb cells 9/13) is CLOSED as completed by PR #1034; the only open docs child of #775 is #845, scoped to citation hypotheses (OPQ-371..376). Severity kept at medium: documentation only, no library defect, and the tutorial's own bound-check passes either way (audited 2.04 vs theoretical 298.83) - the harm is that it teaches an unsound way to compute the bound an audit is checked against.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader follows the privacy-auditing tutorial, trains with a shuffled fixed-batch `DataLoader` and computes the 'Theoretical epsilon' with Poisson amplification and floor-divided step count. Reproduced at HEAD with the notebook's constants (n_samples=500, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, noise_multiplier=0.5, delta=1e-5): the training subset is 252 rows, the loader yields 4 batches/epoch = 800 steps, the notebook reports 600. Published epsilon 250.89 vs 314.46 at the true step count vs 519.70 under the honest unamplified model for a deterministic shuffled partition. The notebook is not in the pr.yml execution list, so nothing detects either error; its committed outputs (263-row subset, theoretical eps 298.83) were produced by an older tree.

verdicts.title: "Documented privacy examples execute in CI" is a partial check: no markdown snippet runs, 4 of 7 tutorials are never executed, and no published notebook output is ever diffed against a fresh run
verdicts.reasoning: Every sub-claim checked at HEAD. (a) `.github/workflows/pr.yml:290-302` is the whole 'Execute accounting documentation' step: `examples/quickstart.py`, `python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`, and `jupyter execute` on copies of 3 notebooks. (b) 369 ```python fences across 46 docs/*.md files; `grep -n doctest pyproject.toml conftest.py .github/workflows/*.yml` returns only that one pr.yml line - no doctest-glob, no markdown harness, so zero markdown snippets execute. (c) `ls docs/tutorials/*.ipynb` -> 7; the step names 3; distributed_training, llm_finetuning, privacy_auditing and sampling_and_microbatching are never executed. (d) 8 files in examples/, only quickstart.py runs. (e) `-m doctest -v` prints '4 tests in 1 items, 4 passed', and all four lines (accounting/__init__.py:19-22) are bare statements with 'Expecting nothing' - it is an import smoke test with no numeric assertion. (f) mkdocs.yml:59-61 sets `mkdocs-jupyter: execute: false`, and pr.yml copies each notebook to $RUNNER_TEMP before `--inplace`, so the repo copy is never rewritten or diffed; the site serves committed outputs that CI never compares to a fresh run. (g) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no docs job at all (jobs: rust-tests, python-tests-*, qodana, build/validate/merge/publish) - the check exists only on PRs. Drift reproduced exactly: sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb publishes 'Poisson -- mean: 32.0, std: 5.5, max: 47' and 'Poisson: epsilon = 3.8331'; HEAD produces 32.4 / 6.1 / 51 and 3.8333. Supporting context I verified: closed issue #843's acceptance criteria were 'Every documented accounting and training snippet executes as written, in CI' and 'The executable-docs check runs on every PR, so this class cannot recur silently' - neither holds. Severity lowered to low: this is a coverage/process gap with no user-visible defect of its own; the demonstrated numeric drift is 4th-decimal, and the substantive consequences (findings 124 and 126) are reported separately, so counting them again here would double-count. Not tracked: open #417 is a performance-benchmark harness ('impact: performance', restoring throughput/memory claims), not docs-snippet execution; open #845 is citations only.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The CI step added by PR #1034 covers one example script, an assertion-free 4-line doctest, and 3 of 7 tutorials, executed in $RUNNER_TEMP so published outputs are never compared to a fresh run; it does not exist on pushes to main. Consequently 369 markdown snippets across 46 docs pages and 4 tutorials have no gate. Demonstrated drift at HEAD: sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb publishes 32.0/5.5/47 batch-size stats and epsilon 3.8331 where the current code yields 32.4/6.1/51 and 3.8333, and privacy_auditing.ipynb publishes a 263-row training subset where the current code yields 252. The magnitudes are cosmetic; the material consequence is that genuinely wrong documented snippets (the unexecutable BSR accounting call, the Poisson-priced shuffled-loader audit tutorial) can and do sit in the published docs unnoticed.

verdicts.title: BSR mechanism page's accounting snippet raises TypeError and its parameter tables document strategy/accounting parameters that do not exist
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced directly. `inspect.signature(opaque.dpftrl.noise.bsr_strategy)` is `(*, bandwidth: int, alpha: float, beta: float) -> BsrStrategy`; the docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bsr.md:21-27 call `bsr_strategy(bandwidth=8, n_steps=total_steps, min_sep=steps_per_epoch, max_participations=num_epochs, alpha=1.0, beta=0.95)` raises `TypeError: bsr_strategy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_steps'` on the first statement of the page's only accounting recipe. The 'Strategy parameters' table at bsr.md:43-45 lists n_steps / min_sep / max_participations as strategy parameters; none is accepted. The 'Accounting parameters' table at bsr.md:52-54 lists `sensitivity` and `gram_matrix`, but `balls_in_bins(inner, *, num_bins, n_steps)` takes neither and `BsrStrategy.gram_matrix` is a method, not an attribute (verified: `type(getattr(s,'gram_matrix'))` is `method`). The page contradicts itself - the noise snippet at bsr.md:63-76 uses the correct `bsr_strategy(bandwidth=8, alpha=1.0, beta=0.95)` and passes n_steps/min_sep/max_participations to `mf_gaussian_noise`, which does accept them. Sibling pages are right and explicit about the split: bisr.md:17-20 and lambda-cgd.md:16-22 say the strategy is a recipe and the amplifier supplies horizon and participation pattern, and bisr.md separates 'Strategy parameters' from 'Amplifier and accounting parameters'. Corrected form verified end to end: `balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, bsr_strategy(bandwidth=8, alpha=1.0, beta=0.95)), num_bins=100, n_steps=500).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 37.93, so only the strategy call is wrong. Not tracked (#844, the reference-tables sweep, is closed; #845 is citations). Severity lowered to low: documentation only, fails loudly on the first line rather than silently, no epsilon impact - dropping the three arguments yields the correct number because the balls_in_bins amplifier already supplies the participation geometry.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader copies the only accounting recipe on the published BSR page and gets `TypeError: bsr_strategy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_steps'` immediately (reproduced verbatim at HEAD). The page's 'Strategy parameters' table repeats the same three non-existent parameters and its 'Accounting parameters' table lists `sensitivity` and `gram_matrix`, which `balls_in_bins(inner, *, num_bins, n_steps)` does not accept. Removing the three arguments gives the correct result (eps 37.93 for bandwidth=8, alpha=1.0, beta=0.95, num_bins=100, n_steps=500), so the cost is a loud failure plus misinformation about which object owns the participation geometry - not a wrong epsilon.

verdicts.title: Paired second-moment accounting is documented as unconditionally equal to the first-moment mechanism, but the runtime sizes both streams from single-participation column norms
verdicts.reasoning: The defect is real and larger than claimed, but its specific criterion and magnitude are wrong, and the code half is already tracked. Verified: (1) docs/reference/accounting.md:330-338 asserts 'privacy accounting is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism' with no condition, docs/reference/noise.md:83-90 and docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md:176-178 repeat it, and the derivation there is stated in terms of the single-participation column norms (Delta1 = zeta*||C1||, Delta2 = zeta^2*||C2||). (2) The Mahalanobis identity itself holds exactly: paired_noise_stddevs(1.3, first=0.7, second=0.49) gives sum (Delta/sigma)^2 = 0.5917159763313609 = 1/nm^2 to the last bit. (3) _second_moment.py:138-149 computes c1 and c2 at `min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1` (single participation) and passes `noise_multiplier/c1`; confirmed at runtime that the paired first-stream base sigma is exactly sqrt(2) x the single-stream sigma when D1=D2. (4) Nothing validates the pairing: `mf_gaussian_noise(params, lambda_cgd_strategy(0.9), second_moment_strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(0.999), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10, noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0))` constructs and runs with zero warnings, and the only invariant test (tests/noise/test_second_moment_noise.py:194-234) pins the identity solely at min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 - the case where the code is correct. WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: its exhibited pair proves nothing. The DP-FTRL poisson and b_min_sep accountants both normalize by the SINGLE-participation sensitivity (_poisson.py:181-185 and _b_min_sep/__init__.py:166-171 call sensitivity(min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) and price repeats by composition/transcript DP), so band_mf pairs raise no rho mismatch there at all, and BandMfStrategy has no gram_matrix (balls_in_bins refuses it). Its rho values come from `sensitivity()`, which for BISR is a conservative majorization: bisr(bandwidth=4).sensitivity(n=1000, min_sep=100, max_part=10) = 3.8106 but its actual BnB Gram diagonal is exactly 10.0, i.e. a true blow-up of sqrt(10) = 3.1623, identical to band_mf(10)'s - so the claimed '~11% higher realized sensitivity' is an artifact of a conservative bound, not an excess. The real criterion for the BnB-accounted families is dominance of the normalized Gram, and the real magnitude is much worse. Derived and numerically validated: the paired release's BnB dominating pair has Gram [D1*G1/c1^2 + D2*G2/c2^2]*c1^2/(D1+D2) while balls_in_bins prices G1; with clipping_norm=1.0 the clipper emits max_norm=C/B and squared_max_norm=C^2/B (clipping/_clipped_fun.py:391-393), so D1=D2 and the realized Gram is (G1+G2)/2. My harness reproduces the public accounted value exactly (14.9990 = balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, lambda_cgd(0.9)), num_bins=100, n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)), and the realized epsilon for the same release paired with lambda_cgd(0.99) is 21.01 (+40%) and with lambda_cgd(0.999) is 40.47 (+170%). That pairing mirrors the pattern the docs themselves recommend (user-guide/optimizers.md:245-247 and user-guide/noise.md:282-284 pair momentum 0.9 for the first moment with 0.999 for the second, and noise.md:305 says the squared-gradient workload 'can differ'), and lambda-cgd.md:71 tells lambdaCGD users to pass second_moment_strategy explicitly without saying which. ALREADY TRACKED: open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments consistently', severity high, blocked/needs-design) states the same defect in its problem statement - 'Paired second-moment allocation also mixes single- and multi-participation sensitivities' - with the acceptance criterion 'Runtime first/second-moment allocation and accounting use the same deployed sensitivities'. The only delta is that the reference docs now assert the equality as settled; that is a documentation overstatement on top of #359, not a new defect. Severity high (matching #359) rather than medium: the epsilon understatement is silent and large, but it needs an explicitly-passed, mismatched second_moment_strategy, so not critical.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With DP-FTRL private second moments, `mf_gaussian_noise` sizes both streams from single-participation column norms (c1, c2 computed at min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) while the balls-in-bins accountant prices the first stream through its multi-participation Gram. The documented accounting recipe (balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, first_strategy), ...), with the reference docs stating accounting 'is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism') is then exact only when the two strategies have the same normalized Gram - which holds trivially when they are identical, and nothing checks it. Established at n_steps=1000, num_bins=100 (10 epochs), clipping_norm=1.0, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5: first=lambda_cgd(0.9) reports eps = 14.999, while the realized paired release has eps = 21.01 with second=lambda_cgd(0.99) (+40%) and eps = 40.47 with second=lambda_cgd(0.999) (+170%). The mismatched pairing is accepted with no warning, and the only regression test for the joint-budget identity covers just max_participations=1. The finding's own example (band_mf(10) + bisr(4), '~11%') does not reproduce: band_mf is accounted by poisson/b_min_sep, which normalize at single participation, and bisr(4)'s true blow-up equals band_mf(10)'s - its sensitivity() value of 3.81 is a conservative bound. The code defect is the one already tracked as open issue #359; the new element is only that docs/reference/accounting.md:336-338 and docs/reference/noise.md:85-90 now present the equality as unconditional.
